standard_prerequisites.name: Wedderburn's theorem
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of the algebra as a matrix algebra over a skew field finite over the ground field.

standard_prerequisites.name: Centralizers commute with tensor products
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the center of the matrix algebra is the tensor product of the ground field with the center of the skew field, which identifies the center.

core_obligations: The reduction (proof lines 415-419): by the structure theorem the algebra is a matrix algebra over a skew field finite over the ground field, whose center is a field containing the ground field.

The identification of the center (proof lines 420-422): the cited lemma on centralizers of tensor products identifies the center of the matrix algebra with the tensor product of the ground field and the center of the skew field, which is a field and a finite extension of the ground field.
proof_roadmap: Write the algebra as a matrix algebra over a skew field.
Identify its center using the centralizer computation for tensor products.
Use that the center of a skew field is a field to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the center of a finite simple algebra over a field is a finite field extension of the ground field (statement lines 409-413). The proof is a complete argument: the structure theorem writes the algebra as a matrix algebra over a skew field finite over the ground field (proof lines 415-419), and the lemma on centralizers of tensor products identifies the center of that matrix algebra with the tensor product of the ground field and the center of the skew field, which is a field because the center of a skew field is a field (proof lines 420-422). The non-formal content is the identification of the center. The claim is H2.
